premises.text: People attend events to learn from content and to socialize; livestreams, webinars, and AMAs deliver content but not socialization
premises.evidence_span: People come to events for two reasons. To learn from great content and to socialize with people

premises.text: Virtual venue platform with customized avatars lets hundreds of real people move around and talk as at an in-person event, including post-panel socialization
premises.evidence_span: Enter Teo, a platform for virtual events. You appear inside of a venue

premises.text: Monetize by charging organizations a monthly venue fee plus a percentage of ticket sales and virtual sponsorship
premises.evidence_span: charging organizations a monthly fee to have access to our venues. And then we also take a percentage of ticket sales and virtual sponsorship

value.text: Connect distributed communities by delivering both event learning and in-venue socialization online
value.evidence_span: help connect your community, ah, your distributed community

causal_links.evidence_span: The world is missing a product that gives the two benefits of why we are all here at this event online
Creating connections that you could never create otherwise
The way that we make money as a company is by charging organizations a monthly fee to have access to our venues

notes: Livestream/webinar/AMA limitations folded into one missing-socialization pain (rule 6). Avatar movement, stage, and multi-hour socializing treated as cascade of one virtual-venue mechanism. Anti-template: need, product, and monetization separately revisable.
